subject: How does chunksize affect to the data?

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: How does chunksize affect to the data?
parts:
Hi all,

My question is about chunksize argument. I thought that chunksize only affects to the size of the blocks to process the data. Then I thought that changing the chunksize, the output would be the same, the unique difference should be the time spent in process the data and the number of blocks processed. But I tried the function g.calibrate in the same file with chunksizes = 1; and = 0.2, respectively and I obtained different offset and scale coefficients. Why does it happen? 

Any help is more than welcome!

Best,
Jairo

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] How does chunksize affect to the data?
parts: Argument chunksize defines how big the blocks of data are that are loaded. The function g.calibrate stops when a certain hours of data are loaded as specified by minloadcrit and when the calibration criteria are met as explained in the paper. However, g.calibrate can only stop after an integer number of X hour blocks as defined by chunksize. If chunksizes are large it can load much more data then what you specified in minloadcrit. Therefore, chunksize setting can influence how much data is used and the data usage could impacts on the resulting calibration correction coefficients. A higher minloadcrit will typically result in more data and therefore more robust coefficients. To avoid working with unreliable correction coefficients, always check the calibration error indicator post calibration. My guideline would be to not work with data with an calibration error post calibration of 0.01g or higher.
